newsitem.title: FRANCE: French government opposes planned EU farm reform.
newsitem.headline: French government opposes planned EU farm reform.

text.p: France's farm minister Louis Le Pensec on Wednesday urged the European Commission to make serious changes to its planned farm reform, saying it would be a sign of weakness towards the U.S. to cut farm prices ahead of the next round of World Trade Organisation (WTO) talks.

"They must seriously work on a new draft. Brussels wants an overall cut in prices. But is it in the interest of Europe to continue dismantling its farm policy ahead of the next round of negotiations with the United States?...We must remain vigilant," he told French afternoon daily Le Monde.

Le Pensec said that by making voluntary price cuts ahead of the talks the EU might be forced into making further concessions to its trade partners om import tariffs or on the terms for access to EU markets.
But the EU contends that it is better to introduce reforms first, before risking being attacked in international negotiations.
The plan, called Agenda 2000, aims to make farmers more competitive ahead of the 1999 global trade talks and EU expansion eastwards early next century.
On Tuesday European farm ministers, who face angry farmers at home, attacked the EU plan during an informal dinner debate in Brussels.
Agenda 2000 calls for cuts of up to 30 percent in the prices guaranteed to EU farmers and a gradual shift in farm support towards direct payments to farmers.
